name: Seagull Collar
summary: A collar variant financing a put spread with a short call (or a call spread with a short put) so that part of the upside is bought back - a three-leg structure that keeps a slice of the tail.

legs.strike_rule: 0.08-0.12 delta, well above the short call - restores upside participation above it

max_profit: capped between the short and long call strikes, then participating again above the long call strike: effectively (short call strike - basis) x 100 plus everything above the long call strike
max_loss: (share basis - put strike + net debit) x 100
breakevens: share basis + net debit per share
when_to_use: Holding shares that could melt up (a takeover candidate, a momentum name) where a plain collar's hard cap is unacceptable, but downside protection is still required.
entry_rules: Long put 0.30-0.40 delta; short call 0.25-0.30 delta; long call 0.08-0.12 delta with at least 10% of spot between the two call strikes.
Short call strike >= basis x 1.05 and >= basis.
All legs same expiry; OI >= 250 each; 4-leg combo.
Only on names with a plausible upside gap scenario - otherwise the long call is wasted premium.
management_rules: Roll all legs together at 21-30 DTE.
If spot passes the short call strike, do NOT panic-roll; the long call is already restoring delta above its strike.
Monetize the long call if it reaches 4x its cost and re-strike higher.
exit_rules: HARD: the short call is the only assignable leg - flatten it by 15:30 ET on expiration day if ITM; immediate close when extrinsic < 0.05 and delta > 0.85; ex-dividend guard applies.
If the short call is assigned, the shares are delivered and the remaining long put + long call is a long straddle-ish position - close it the same session unless explicitly re-authorized.
Close ITM long options rather than letting them auto-exercise.
assignment_risk: One assignable leg (the short call), covered by the shares. The structural hazard is what remains AFTER assignment: orphaned long options with a directional profile the system did not intend.
buying_power: Shares plus net debit; the short call is covered by shares AND by the long call.
liquidity_needs: Four legs on a liquid chain; combined spread <= 12% of net cost.
common_mistakes: Setting the long call so far out that it never pays; paying too much net debit and turning a hedge into a speculation.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
